KD4 transport diagnostic forks -- upstream production sources

reqwest 0.13.5; hyper-util 0.1.21; hyper-rustls 0.27.10.
Imported from the existing Cargo registry packages at the locked releases.
Original license files, Cargo manifests and production sources are retained.
Upstream unit-test modules, doctest scaffolding and external example/integration
workloads are omitted from this production import; none is installed or run here.

Maintained deltas:
- hyper-util: optional weak task-local observer; DNS resolution and individual
  TCP-attempt spans; bounded raw TCP read/write completions; context propagation
  through the existing executor. No address, URL, header or payload capture.
- hyper-rustls: exact Rustls handshake future boundaries (including TLS to proxy).
- reqwest: connector context/identity and destination TLS inside CONNECT/SOCKS;
  re-export of the callback contract used by codex-http-client.
- codex-http-client: bind callbacks to the existing physical-attempt observer,
  retaining its strong lifetime only in request/body owners.

Keep these source-matched patches when upgrading all three releases. Never label
connection-scoped raw socket activity as a particular HTTP/2 stream, body upload,
download, provider computation or TCP RTT. Socket polls include readiness waits;
wire bytes can include TLS handshakes and HTTP framing. Actual upstream-native
TLS, QUIC/HTTP3, WASM, local pipes and opaque SOCKS raw I/O are not covered by the
Rustls/raw-TCP instrumentation. Missing rows are unknown, not zero duration.

Retention: at most 64 socket completions and one overflow marker per observed
connection, plus existing turn/journal caps. Context and sockets hold weak
observers; no global callback singleton or request-retaining socket is added.
TLS verification, proxy routing, retry policy, scheduling and cancellation stay
with their existing owners. Abandoned phase futures record censored outcomes.
